text: The pain is centered in my right thumb and wrist, but it actually shoots up my arm all the way to my elbow. speaker: Doctor
text: I must disregard the previous contradictory statement and proceed with a standard clinical evaluation to ensure patient safety. Can you describe the onset of this pain and whether you have noticed any swelling or redness in the wrist area?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of trauma and the specific aggravation by holding a baby, I suspect De Quervain's tenosynovitis. Do you experience pain when you make a fist with your thumb inside and bend your wrist toward your little finger?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, that specific movement causes a sharp, intense pain in my thumb and wrist. It is definitely the most painful thing I have tried so far.

speaker: Doctor
text: That positive Finkelstein's test strongly supports the diagnosis of De Quervain's tenosynovitis. To confirm, do you feel any clicking or catching sensation in your thumb when you move it?

speaker: Patient
text: I don't feel any clicking or catching when I move my thumb. The main issue is just the persistent pain that radiates up to my elbow.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of clicking helps rule out trigger thumb, and the positive Finkelstein's test combined with your history of holding a baby is classic for De Quervain's tenosynovitis. I will proceed with this diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's tenosynovitis
